---
title: "qdaR"
---


You have coded material in Zotero with [zotQDA](https://zotqda.org) and now
want to do something with it that the [qdaZ](https://qdaz.zotqda.org) plugin does not offer: combine
several exports, put a figure into a manuscript, run a statistical test
that qdaZ deliberately leaves out, or simply keep the whole analysis in a
reproducible script that still runs next year. That is what qdaR is for.

qdaR is first of all the R-based analysis half of the
**zotQDA ecosystem**: it reads the CSV tables zotQDA exports, and with
those its full range is available.

qdaR also reads **REFI-QDA** projects. A study kept in MAXQDA, ATLAS.ti,
NVivo, QDA Miner or Dedoose can be extended with the metrics and figures
those programs do not (yet) offer: confidence intervals on agreement, the
segmentation measures, saturation as a reportable number, sample-size
planning. Compared to the CSV tables zotQDA exports, a `.qdpx` carries
only a subset. [Reading a .qdpx](guide/qdpx.qmd) lays out both — the
subset and what each program gains through qdaR.

::: {.callout-warning title="Early public beta"}

qdaR is in an **early public beta**. It is published, installable and
documented — and it is not finished:

- **There will be errors.**
- **Interfaces will very likely change** between releases, because the
  code is still being reworked.
- **Correctness of the results cannot be guaranteed.**

Check what you rely on, and pin a version in work that has to be
reproducible. Reports of errors, or of things that get in your way, are
welcome.

The Python twin [qdaPy](https://qdapy.zotqda.org) is at the same stage;
the two Zotero plugins are a step behind it, in a private alpha.
:::

```r
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("easyqda/qdaR")
```

```r
library(qdaR)

frag <- qda_read_fragments("easyqda-fragments.csv")
qda_code_counts(frag)
qda_plot_frequencies(frag)
```

The package documentation — every function with its arguments and
examples — comes with the installation: `help(package = "qdaR")`, and
`vignette("qdaR")` for a worked run through the whole thing.

## What qdaR does not do

qdaR codes nothing and never writes back to Zotero. Coding happens in
zotQDA; qdaR only reads what zotQDA exported, analyses it statistically
and illustrates the data.

If a result in qdaR differs from the one in the qdaZ plugin, that is a
bug worth reporting, not a matter of opinion. The two libraries are
tested against each other on shared reference data.

It also will not decide your method for you. Several functions ask you to
make a decision the code cannot make on your behalf, and say so in their
documentation rather than picking a default that flatters the result.
